STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square/rectangular white plate (rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plate type: 20-30 cm; this one looks like a medium-large dinner plate, about 25 cm square.
b) Reference: the chicken drumstick is about 11 cm long. Across the plate width (the long axis of the drumstick runs roughly 2 drumstick-lengths from the top-right corner to the plate edge), the plate spans about 2.3 drumstick lengths, giving about 25 cm.
Final width: 25 cm square, area 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Pizza: 2 slices visible, each about 11 x 11 cm with 1.5 cm thickness. Footprint per slice ~ 121 cm² (for a bread-like slice, count-based: 2 slices x 30 g). Using the countable rule: 2 slices x 30 g... slice of pizza is heavier, so estimate 2 x 60 g = 120 g (cheese and sauce included).
- Caesar-style salad (romaine with dressing): footprint ~18% of 625 = 112 cm², mound averaging 3 cm thick, so volume ~340 ml; cooked-to-raw leafy greens with dressing, use 0.3 g/ml -> ~100 g.
- Chicken drumstick: 1 piece, 90 g (skin, sauce on it).
- Second meat piece (dark, breaded/crumbed, roughly 6 x 5 cm, 2.5 cm thick): ~ 50 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer under the pizza or salad; the salad sits on the plate directly. No extra hidden items counted.

STEP 5 - Energy values per 100 g (as served):
- Pizza (cheese and tomato, baked): ~270 kcal
- Caesar salad with dressing: ~150 kcal
- Chicken drumstick (skin on, roasted): ~200 kcal
- Breaded/crumbed meat piece: ~250 kcal

Total weight ≈ 120 + 100 + 90 + 50 = 360 g. Total energy ≈ 324 + 150 + 180 + 125 ≈ 780 kcal.
